extracted.intended_audience: members of the London Mathematical Society; UK and international mathematicians, researchers, postgraduate students, and organisers of mathematical meetings
extracted.subtask_short: LMS newsletter event and submission guidelines
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural guidance, eligibility rules, deadlines, and formatting/organisation requirements for LMS/related events, proposals, workshops, fellowships, nominations and short courses as published in the LMS Newsletter (No.336, April 2005).

rubrics_metrics.name: Council nomination requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Normal nominations to Council are made via the Nominating Committee, but there is provision for members to make nominations directly. Anyone who wishes to propose someone for a position as an Officer of the Society or as a member of Council is invited to inform E.G. Rees (Nominating Committee chair) by 13 May 2005. Direct nominations should be sent to the Executive Secretary to arrive before 1 September 2005, before noon. Such nominations must bear the signatures of the Nominator and three Seconders and of the Nominee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact details given (E.Rees@ed.ac.uk for Nominating Committee; cooper@lms.ac.uk for Executive Secretary). The Nominating Committee members are listed for reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICMS workshop proposal submission and selection guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are invited for workshops to be held at the International Centre for Mathematical Sciences (ICMS). Potential organisers should contact ICMS early to discuss ideas. The proposal document should not normally exceed five pages and should be submitted electronically (PDF, PS, Word or DVI). Proposals may be submitted at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICMS particularly welcomes proposals for rapidly-developing areas (R3WP). Organisers can expect preliminary comments from reviewers in 8 weeks. Decisions will be made by the Programme Committee four times a year (December, March, May and September). Small meetings can be organised in 6–8 months from acceptance. Successful applicants will be offered a funding package to contribute to travel and subsistence of a proportion of participants. ICMS staff will undertake non-scientific administration (issuing invitations, processing registrations, organising accommodation, preparing material, financial administration). One Scientific Organiser will be appointed Principal Organiser and be the main point of contact. Full instructions and refereeing/selection criteria are on the ICMS web pages (www.icms.org.uk/call/index.html).

rubrics_metrics.name: MAFELAP mini-symposium parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Parameters for a mini-symposium at MAFELAP: a time-slot will be allocated to organisers, during which they can have four speakers, each giving a presentation (probably 30 minutes: 25 minutes talk plus 5 minutes for questions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If organisers want more than four talks then two two-hour slots could be given. Interested organisers should submit a title to the MAFELAP Secretary with a tentative list of speakers as soon as possible (contact mafelap2006@brunel.ac.uk).

rubrics_metrics.name: BA Media Fellowship eligibility and scheme details
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility for the BA Media Fellowship Scheme: you are eligible to apply if you are a scientist, social scientist or engineer and have a minimum of two years postgraduate experience in your field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowships are summer placements of three to eight weeks with media organisations to learn how science is reported. Host organisations have included The Guardian, BBC Radio, Nature Online and Countryfile. Additional eligibility fragments in the notice indicate applicants should be a UK citizen and may work at any level in an academic or research institution, industry, civil service or similar organisation. For further information and online application visit www.the-ba.net/mediafellows.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICMS Coagulation–Fragmentation workshop application deadlines and contributed-talk rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for the ICMS Coagulation-Fragmentation Processes workshop should be submitted (see website for online form). Applications and payment should normally be received by Monday 6 June. Anyone wishing to be considered for a contributed talk should complete their application by Monday 2 May.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The meeting expects to invite around twenty 30-minute contributed talks and will include a poster session. See the workshop webpage for details and use the online application form. Contact details for the organising committee are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: LMS/EPSRC short course application, audience and funding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Short courses (e.g. Nonlinear Wave Phenomena; Algebraic Topology) state target audience and application rules: courses are aimed at advanced postgraduate students and postdoctoral researchers (or PhD students in Algebraic Topology). Numbers will be limited and those interested are advised to make an early application. Closing dates for applications are given for each course (e.g. Nonlinear Waves closing date Friday 6 May 2005; Algebraic Topology closing date Friday 13 May 2005).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration fee is typically £100. Accommodation costs for all UK-based research students are covered by EPSRC; participants must pay their own travel costs. EPSRC-supported students can expect registration fees and travel costs to be met by their departments from the EPSRC Doctoral Training Account. Postdocs and non-UK students will be required to pay their own subsistence costs. Application forms may be obtained from the LMS Administrative Officer or from the LMS website. All applicants will be contacted approximately one week after the deadline; do not send money until requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isaac Newton Institute satellite meeting application, fees and support
rubrics_metrics.description: Satellite meetings associated with Newton Institute programmes list application procedures, costs and support: application forms and further information are available from the web; specific closing dates are given for particular satellite meetings (e.g. closing date for applications 30 April 2005 for one Newton Institute event).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For some Newton Institute-associated events a Conference Package costing (example) £480 is available and includes accommodation, breakfast and dinner for specified dates plus lunches and refreshments during lecture days. Participants who do not require the Conference Package may be charged a registration fee (example £35). Some financial support is available for younger researchers. Completed application forms should be sent to the named Programme & Conference Secretary (contact details provided). Web links to application pages are supplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Women in Mathematics Day registration and support
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration instructions and support for Women in Mathematics Day: the day is free for postgraduate students and £5 for all others (payable on the day). Limited funds are available to help with travel costs. Postgraduate speakers are invited and organisers encourage women at various career stages to attend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programme times and sessions are listed; those interested in giving a postgraduate talk should contact the named organiser. Registration is via the Administrative Officer (telephone, fax, email provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference registration and publication rules (Kingfisher Delta'05 example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conference organisers set registration and publication rules: for Kingfisher Delta'05, standard registration before 31 August is A$520, with discounts for students and members of the Australian Mathematical Society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full papers accepted by reviewers will appear in the Conference Proceedings (a special double issue of a journal). Short non-refereed papers will be published in Conference Communications. Abstracts will appear in the Conference Handbook. Registration details and discount policies are provided on the conference website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coagulation–Fragmentation workshop intended audience
rubrics_metrics.description: The Coagulation-Fragmentation workshop lists the intended audiences: (i) mathematicians (applied and numerical analysts, probabilists), (ii) physicists and chemists deriving CF equations in applications, and (iii) industrialists and engineers applying CF processes in design and manufacturing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The aim is to bring together theoreticians and practitioners; invited speaker list and organising committee contact details are provided. Applicants should use the website application form and note application deadlines.
